videos.script: OWASP is an open community that writes down how software fails. Its list for applications built on language models has ten entries, and the current edition is from 2025. {{title}} The list is a vocabulary. When a reviewer says excessive agency, everyone in the room should picture the same failure. {{vocabulary}} It is not a checklist you tick once. Each entry is a question to ask of your own application. {{question}} In the lab, the ten entries sit beside the commands this course has built. Eight have at least one control. {{map}} Two have none here. Poisoning, and weaknesses in the vector store a model retrieves from. {{gaps}} A review that uses the list honestly writes that down, with the control it still needs or the risk somebody accepted. {{review}}
